fact_reviews.subject: main/sysdolphin/baselib/leak:HSD_Leak_80387DF8
fact_reviews.old_value: Reads the scan start from `lbCommand_803B9840`, the scan limit from `OSGetConsoleSimulatedMemSize`, the valid physical-address ceiling from `OSGetPhysicalMemSize`, and registration state from `HSD_Leak_80407B58`. Pointer-like words whose derived headers contain `HEAP_MAGIC` and a valid registration index cause the low bit of the matching table entry to be set. The subsequent table pass consumes that bit, clears it, validates remaining entries against their heap headers and registration slots, emits reports through `OSReport`, and returns the accumulated leak count.
fact_reviews.reason: Replace ambiguous or incomplete wording with directly observed behavior and distinguish existing object sizes from canonical source facts.

fact_reviews.subject: main/sysdolphin/baselib/leak:HSD_Leak_80387DF8
fact_reviews.old_value: If the checker table is null, reports an uninitialized state and returns zero. Otherwise it performs two phases. During marking, a table entry changes from unmarked to marked only when a scanned aligned word denotes a valid heap header whose stored registration index selects that same header. During sweeping, marked entries are restored to their unmarked pointer value and accepted as referenced; null entries and pointers into the registration table are ignored; every other entry becomes one reported leak, classified as a valid-header leak when its magic and registration backlink agree or as a destroyed-header leak otherwise. It then reports either the positive leak total or that no leak was detected.
fact_reviews.reason: Canonical code and bounded consumer evidence support the inherited behavior.
